title: FOLFIRI

agents.name: Irinotecan
agents.explanation: The body converts irinotecan into SN-38. This traps an enzyme called topoisomerase I while DNA is being copied, causing damage that can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal bowel and blood-forming cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about cramps, sweating or diarrhoea during the infusion. Diarrhoea starting later needs the separate written treatment and contact plan.
risks: Rare serious lung or allergic reactions

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
agents.watch: The combined treatment can increase mouth soreness and diarrhoea. Report these promptly. Rare allergic reactions can occur.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
agents.watch: Diarrhoea, mouth sores and skin soreness may become serious. Chest pain during the pump infusion needs emergency assessment. Unexpected severe early toxicity can occur even after DPD testing.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

HSE: chemotherapy side effects and urgent advice
eviQ: treatment through an implanted port

questions.q: Does having more side effects mean treatment is working?
questions.a: No. Side effects do not reliably show whether the cancer is responding. Report them so they can be treated. Your team assesses benefit using the tests and review plan appropriate to your cancer.

questions.q: Why might a dose be delayed or reduced?
questions.a: Your team may allow recovery, investigate a symptom or reduce the chance of lasting harm. Ask which drug changes, why, and when review is planned. A delay does not itself mean treatment has failed.

questions.q: What should I say when calling?
questions.a: Give the regimen name, last treatment date, symptoms and when they started. Explain whether you can eat, drink, pass urine and manage usual activities. Give your temperature if available, but do not delay calling to collect details.

questions.q: What belongs in the consent conversation?
questions.a: The individual aim and likely benefit, uncertainty, reasonable alternatives including not proceeding, common and serious risks, lasting effects, fertility and practical concerns. You can ask for an interpreter, more time or another explanation and can reconsider your decision.

questions.q: How many cycles should I use this passport for?
questions.a: The passport provides reusable recording pages, not a prescribed course length. Your oncology team sets the duration and can provide extra pages.

questions.q: Will I need a port or a PICC?
questions.a: The team chooses the most suitable access device with you. A port is under the skin; a PICC enters through the upper arm and has an external section. Both require specific care, and the pump can be used with either.

questions.q: Does disconnecting the pump remove my port?
questions.a: No. At the arranged visit the pump is disconnected and the line cared for. A port needle may be removed, but the implanted port stays under the skin until a separate removal procedure is arranged.

questions.q: What if the pump finishes early or still looks full?
questions.a: Contact the team for advice. Do not change delivery settings or disconnect or reconnect it yourself. Follow only the specific emergency steps you have been taught.

questions.q: Is delayed diarrhoea the same as cramps during infusion?
questions.a: No. Irinotecan can cause an early reaction with cramps, sweating or diarrhoea, and a later diarrhoea problem. Tell the nurse about early symptoms and follow the separate written plan at home.

phases_note: Treatment is reviewed against benefit, side effects and your priorities. Reductions, breaks or a maintenance plan are individual decisions, not an automatic change after a set number of cycles.
medicines_title: Your medicines and what they do
timeline_note: Bars show planned treatment and possible symptom patterns, not measured risk. Side effects can overlap and persist.
safety_note: There are no guaranteed safe days. Act on fever, sudden illness or a new serious symptom whenever it occurs. Do not wait for the next appointment.
teachback: Can you explain which medicines you are receiving, the schedule, the contact plan and the symptoms that need prompt help?
consent_support: Confirm DPD testing, anti-sickness medicines, port/PICC care, the 46-hour pump and disconnection arrangements. Explain early cholinergic symptoms and the separate delayed-diarrhoea plan.
urgent_extra: Contact promptly for new chest symptoms, severe or persistent diarrhoea, reduced urine, inability to drink, severe abdominal pain or a line/pump problem.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim and review plan
chapters.intro: Ask what treatment is intended to achieve for you.

items.title: Confirm the cancer setting
items.text: FOLFIRI combines irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil. NCCP 00227 covers advanced colorectal cancer, metastatic oesophageal cancer and second-line advanced pancreatic cancer. Your team confirms your indication and treatment aim.

items.title: Review rather than a fixed promise
items.text: Ask when scans and clinical review will assess benefit. Treatment may be adjusted if it is not helping or side effects outweigh benefit. A cycle delay is not itself proof that treatment has stopped working.

items.title: Your priorities matter
items.text: Discuss symptoms you want to improve, daily activities, work, caring responsibilities and time at home. The team can explain alternatives and how they compare in your situation.

chapters.title: Bowel symptoms: act early
chapters.intro: Keep the written plan with your medicines.

items.title: During the infusion
items.text: With irinotecan, sudden cramps, sweating, a runny nose or diarrhoea can occur during or soon after treatment. Tell the nurse immediately; this needs a different approach from delayed diarrhoea.

items.title: At home
items.text: Record changes from your usual bowel pattern or stoma output. Follow your prescribed diarrhoea plan and contact oncology if symptoms persist or you cannot replace lost fluids. Do not wait for the next scheduled visit.

items.title: Get urgent advice
items.text: Fever, severe pain, blood in stools, dizziness, reduced urine or inability to drink alongside diarrhoea needs urgent assessment. Severe abdominal pain must not be assumed to be an ordinary treatment effect.

chapters.title: Tests and preparation
chapters.intro: Checks support safe treatment even when you feel well.

items.title: Blood tests and symptoms
items.text: The team reviews blood counts, kidney and liver function and symptoms before another cycle. Missing information is not assumed to be normal.

items.title: DPD and fluorouracil
items.text: DPD helps the body break down fluorouracil. Deficiency can cause severe toxicity. Testing guides the plan but cannot exclude all serious reactions; unexpectedly severe early diarrhoea, mouth sores or illness needs immediate review.

items.title: Additional checks
items.text: Tell the team about liver disease, previous severe diarrhoea, heart problems and all medicines. Irinotecan handling can differ between people; any additional testing is decided by your team.

chapters.title: Eating, activity and daily life
chapters.intro: Choose manageable steps and ask for help early.

items.title: Food and fluids
items.text: Take prescribed anti-sickness medicines. Small regular meals may be easier when appetite is low. Tell the team if vomiting, mouth soreness or diarrhoea prevents enough intake; follow any fluid restriction you have.

items.title: Activity and rest
items.text: Short, comfortable activity and planned rests can help you organise the day. Avoid activity that pulls the line or risks damaging the pump. Ask about work, driving and travel around your own treatment and symptoms.

items.title: Sex, fertility and pregnancy
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment where relevant. Ask about contraception, pregnancy, breastfeeding and precautions around sex during treatment; the required precautions depend on the medicines.

chapters.title: Medicines and supportive care
chapters.intro: Bring a complete list, including supplements.

items.title: Before adding medicines
items.text: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter products and supplements with the oncology pharmacist. Do not independently stop regular medicines such as anticoagulants before a procedure.

items.title: Supportive prescriptions
items.text: Keep anti-sickness medicines and the bowel-symptom plan accessible. If growth-factor injections are prescribed, confirm when they are due in relation to the pump; do not infer timing from the graph.

items.title: Treatment changes
items.text: Ask which medicine is being delayed, reduced or stopped and why. Each medicine can change separately; record the agreed plan in your own treatment documents.

chapters.title: Prepare for the next conversation
chapters.intro: You do not have to remember everything.

items.title: Bring your questions
items.text: Use the passport to note symptoms and their effect on eating, drinking, sleep and everyday tasks. You do not need to work out which medicine caused them.

items.title: Ask for practical support
items.text: Ask for a written appointment and contact plan, an interpreter if needed, and help for a family member or carer learning the pump instructions.

items.title: Tell us what was unclear
items.text: Ask the nurse to demonstrate the pump and line, then explain back when and how you would seek help. More explanation is appropriate whenever you need it.

purpose: FOLFIRI combines irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil. NCCP 00227 covers advanced colorectal cancer, metastatic oesophageal cancer and second-line advanced pancreatic cancer. Your team confirms your indication and treatment aim.
schedule_summary: Day 1: irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. A cycle lasts 14 days; your team confirms the next treatment.

phases.label: 14-day treatment cycle
phases.detail: Day 1: irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, then a 46-hour fluorouracil pump. A cycle lasts 14 days; your team confirms the next treatment.

timeline.label: Delayed diarrhoea
timeline.text: Can start after 24 hours; report early

timeline.label: Blood counts / infection
timeline.text: Timing varies; no guaranteed safe days

day_groups.title: Infusion and pump connection
day_groups.body: The team reviews symptoms, blood results and your treatment plan. Day-ward infusions are followed by connection of the fluorouracil pump.
day_groups.action: Before leaving, confirm the pump-care instructions, disconnection appointment and contact number.

day_groups.title: The pump is delivering treatment
day_groups.body: The pump runs for approximately 46 hours from connection. Keep it and the line secure and dry as taught. The team confirms the actual disconnection appointment.
day_groups.action: Call for a leaking, disconnected or unexpectedly stopped pump. Do not reconnect, alter settings or disconnect it yourself unless specifically trained and instructed.

day_groups.title: After disconnection
day_groups.body: Delayed diarrhoea can begin after the first 24 hours and may continue after the pump is removed. Use the written plan and contact the team early. Mouth soreness, nausea and tiredness can overlap.
day_groups.action: Report poor intake, persistent diarrhoea or mouth pain early. Chest pain or major breathing difficulty requires emergency help.

day_groups.title: Between visits and the next review
day_groups.body: Blood counts can fall between visits. Tell the team about bowel symptoms, mouth pain and how you are managing daily activities. Treatment proceeds only after review.
day_groups.action: Bring the symptom passport and check the next appointment. Day 1 usually repeats 14 days after this cycle started, only if confirmed.

support.title: DPD testing before fluorouracil
support.text: DPD helps the body break down fluorouracil. Deficiency can cause severe toxicity. Testing guides the plan but cannot exclude all serious reactions; unexpectedly severe early diarrhoea, mouth sores or illness needs immediate review.

support.title: Your diarrhoea plan
support.text: Have the prescribed anti-diarrhoeal medicine and written instructions before going home. Follow that plan as soon as diarrhoea starts. Call promptly for persistent symptoms, cramps, fever, blood in stools or reduced urine.

support.title: Pump and line care
support.text: See “Your port and treatment pump” for insertion, connection, daily care and disconnection. Before leaving, know who to call, where to return and how to use the supplied spill plan.

support.title: Anti-sickness support
support.text: Take prescribed preventive medicines and keep the breakthrough plan available. Some anti-sickness medicines cause constipation. Ask for review if symptoms are poorly controlled.

evidence.title: What a colorectal trial tells us
evidence.intro: These results concern previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer, not every cancer indication for FOLFIRI.
evidence.population: GERCOR randomised 220 patients to FOLFIRI followed by FOLFOX6 or the reverse sequence. The figures show first-line tumour response.

metrics.label: Tumours that shrank enough to meet response criteria

evidence.interpretation: These response rates are not cure rates. The study did not establish a survival advantage for one sequence. It does not predict individual benefit, or validate the oesophageal or pancreatic indications.

chronology_notes.title: Day ward and home pump
chronology_notes.text: Day 1 infusions lead into a 46-hour pump. The team confirms the disconnection appointment.

chronology_notes.title: Two types of diarrhoea
chronology_notes.text: Cramps and sweating during infusion need immediate nursing attention. Later diarrhoea needs your written home plan and early contact.

chronology_notes.title: No safe window
chronology_notes.text: Fever or sudden illness needs prompt action on any day, including after pump removal.

chronology_notes.title: Between visits
chronology_notes.text: Bowel symptoms, mouth soreness and fatigue can overlap. Describe their effect on eating, drinking and daily tasks.

anatomy: Hair thinning or loss may occur. Ask about support.
Report ulcers or pain affecting eating and drinking.
New chest pain or breathlessness needs urgent assessment.
Report diarrhoea, increased stoma output or severe abdominal pain.
Report painful redness, peeling or loss of hand function.
Fever, shivers or sudden illness: call oncology immediately.
Report painful skin changes affecting activity.
Pain, leakage, swelling or poor wound healing needs advice.
